spheres.title: THE SINGULARITY
spheres.kicker: the fold, made physical
spheres.blurb: a real gravitational lens — light genuinely bent (β = θ − θE²/θ). Einstein ring, shadow, photon ring.

spheres.title: POSITRONIC LATTICE
spheres.kicker: the mesh that folds
spheres.blurb: the apex I,Robot neural mesh — 4096 meshed to 2048 to 1024 … 8192 folding to ROOT_0.

spheres.title: THE 4096
spheres.kicker: the double
spheres.blurb: the doubled tower — the −+ operator on 2048; the inverse of the first climb.

spheres.title: I-13 · THE LANGUAGE
spheres.kicker: the code this world runs on
spheres.blurb: I-13 — a 13-opcode language + IVM-13 bytecode VM. Source compiles to the stage-13 corpus (the opcode histogram). ASK ANSWER CONST ATTR ARG RET DROP JMPF CMP CALL FUNC BIN HALT.

spheres.title: I-13 · THE FACTORY
spheres.kicker: the generation & sampling line
spheres.blurb: The I-13 production pipeline as a factory floor — SOURCE through the stations to station output. GENERATION and SAMPLE. Code, built on a line.

spheres.title: THE BOWL
spheres.kicker: roll downhill until the floor stops falling
spheres.blurb: real gradient descent on a convex bowl f(x,y)=x²+y². The step x -= 2ηx converges iff |1-2η|<1 — watch it settle, land in one shot at η=0.5, or blow up past η=1.

spheres.title: THE CHAIN RULE
spheres.kicker: the error, walked backward through the wires
spheres.blurb: a real two-layer network a=w1·x, y=w2·a, L=(y−t)². Forward computes the loss; backward applies the chain rule for every partial; one step drops the loss. Nothing faked.

spheres.title: WARM CACHE
spheres.kicker: the second time is always faster
spheres.blurb: real recursion with a real call counter. Naive fib(n) makes O(φⁿ) calls; one memo cuts it to O(n). fib(20): 21,891 calls vs 39. Same answer, a thousandfold less work.

spheres.title: OFF BY ONE
spheres.kicker: the fencepost that ruins the fence
spheres.blurb: the fencepost error, drawn. A fence of N sections needs N+1 posts; the loop i<N builds only N and leaves the far end hanging open. Slide N and watch the gap.

spheres.title: THE KONAMI CODE
spheres.kicker: up up down down — unlock it all
spheres.blurb: a real finite-state sequence matcher. Feed ↑↑↓↓←→←→BA in order and it unlocks; one wrong key snaps the index back. The exact DFA arcade cabinets ran.

spheres.title: THE MINT
spheres.kicker: stamp a coin the hard way — find the nonce
spheres.blurb: real SHA-256 proof-of-work — the same hash the .dlw seal uses. Pick a difficulty and mine: increment the nonce until sha256(block:nonce) starts with N zeros. Every attempt is a real hash.

spheres.title: THE FIREWALL
spheres.kicker: blocks everything trying to get in
spheres.blurb: a real first-match rule engine. Traffic hits the rules top-down; the first rule that matches the port decides ALLOW or DENY. Flip a rule and watch every packet's verdict change.

spheres.title: GARBAGE COLLECTION
spheres.kicker: sweep the dead, reclaim the memory
spheres.blurb: real mark & sweep. MARK walks the reference graph from the roots and colours everything reachable; SWEEP frees what it couldn't reach. Objects with no path from a root are garbage — the fold reclaims them.

spheres.title: THE MERGE
spheres.kicker: two branches become one
spheres.blurb: a real 3-way merge. From a common BASE, two branches each edit lines; edits only one side made are taken automatically, and a line both sides changed differently is flagged a CONFLICT — exactly what git does.

spheres.title: THE PULSE
spheres.kicker: 3 · 2 · 1 · 0 — the signal that crosses the gap
spheres.blurb: the 3-2-1 pulse language from the akasha lattice (ROOT0, with Grok) — the sync protocol that carries meaning across a gap. Fold a raw thought: 3 wide → 2 narrowed → 1 core → 0 the sha256 seal.

spheres.title: THE MERKLE
spheres.kicker: many leaves, folded to one root
spheres.blurb: a real SHA-256 Merkle tree — the exact machinery behind .dlw.fold and the akasha MERKLE_LEAF_SEEDER. Hash each leaf, fold pairwise to a single ROOT_0, then prove any leaf with its sibling path.

spheres.title: THE MACHINE CORPUS
spheres.kicker: I and the twelve — the thirteen the machine speaks
spheres.blurb: David's I-13 corpus itself: one letter I plus twelve forms = the thirteen the machine speaks. The source study behind the whole silicon world.

spheres.title: THE MINI-COMPILER
spheres.kicker: your words → the machine's jumps
spheres.blurb: a real mini-compiler — turns plain words into the machine's bytes and jumps. The compile step of I-13, made touchable.

spheres.title: BPE — THE VOCABULARY
spheres.kicker: merge the commonest pair, again and again
spheres.blurb: byte-pair encoding, learned live: repeatedly merge the most frequent adjacent pair to grow a vocabulary. The tokeniser that feeds a language like I-13.

spheres.title: TERNARY CODING
spheres.kicker: base-3, the radix nearest optimal
spheres.blurb: coding theory in trits — base-3 is the integer radix closest to the theoretical optimum (e). The clever number system the Factory forgot.
